newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual rejects Ahmanson claims.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual rejects Ahmanson claims.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc said Thursday the allegations made by H.F. Ahmanson & Co earlier in the day were "unfounded" and designed to distract shareholders.

"With its latest unfounded 'allegation of the day', Ahmanson is again attempting to distract stockholders and the investment community from the superior value offered by the Washington Mutual/Great Western merger," it said.
"This latest desperate attempt comes on the heels of Great Western's board of directors reaffirming the superiority of Washington Mutual's transaction over Ahmanson's revised hostile bid," it added.
Early Thursday, Ahmanson said it had asked the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate the accounting practices of Washington Mutual.
It said it was not certain whether the financial service company could qualify for the pooling of interests planned for its proposed acquisition of Great Western Financial Corp .
Ahmanson, which also offered to buy Great Western, said it was presenting to the commission material showing that Washington had intended to buy back shares after the acquisition.
Under SEC rules, an intention to buy back shares precludes such a combination from being treated as a pooling of interests for accounting purposes.
Great Western has nevertheless declined to negotiate with Ahmanson.
The financial services company rejected the allegations that it had planned to buy back stock.
"Washington Mutual has never in its history instituted a common stock repurchase program, has never stated an intention to institute such a program, and has no plans to do so in the future," it said.
Washington Mutual has offered to acquire Great Western for $6.6 billion, while Ahmanson's bid is worth $7.0 billion.
